That functional separation reminds me of studies showing text predictors can spontaneously build internal representations of complex game boards and even infer hidden player abilities just from raw sequences. But when you shift that focus to step-by-step problem solving, I’m wondering whether having the model review its own proposed sequences actually helps or just introduces more errors. Specifically, does running iterative self-evaluation during planning tasks tend to degrade the final output quality, and do false confirmation rates change depending on whether the system receives simple yes-or-no checks or detailed critiques?
gold_titles: Can Large Language Models Really Improve by Self-critiquing Their Own Plans?
